additional_info.body:
Ciao Luca,
I took a look at the charger's logs after our conversation yesterday. This is what I found:
In this authentication session, for example, you see two command to authorize sent to the Backend. One is rejected and one accepted, but it is not possible to understand which response refers to which command.
Also right after, further attempts are blocked, until one is accepted:
I admit I have never also seen the screenflow showing this RFID flagged.
Let me proceed like this: I will perform a test on our test charger tomorrow in order to exactly correlate the symptoms (what you see on the screen) with the logs, and I will forward this issue to R&D in order to understand:
If the behavior is intended like this or not
If the RFID is supposed to send multiple requests to the Backend
If it is an issue and has to be corrected or if it cannot be solved and some mitigation is required (new screenflow, new error messages, something like that).
I will provide you further details tomorrow after the test and will redirect the topic to R&D.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0474681-DC/Si-D/IT- [Y2/T3 314182274001] RFID multiple transmission session CRM:03288000218
additional_info.body:
Ciao Valerio, Ciao Luca,
Today I conducted some tests on our Laboratory charger in order to replicate the issue and better understand the behavior seen on site. I summarize here my findings, which I fully explained to Valerio today already.
I will start with saying that the behavior was not replicable, but the different behavior observed allowed me to understand where the issue stands: the error message seen on the screen is triggered by a delay that IPlanet's Backend has in processing every OCPP Authorize request. Let's go point by point:
The error message in the picture below is correctly shown by the charger on the HMI whenever an Authorization is Blocked by the Backend.
From our test, you can see how, whenever the charger sends an Authorize.req to our Backend, the Authorize.conf from the Backend arrives instantaneously:
This is not the case with IPlanet's Backend. You can see in the examples below that the Backend takes 1 second or even more seconds to process the request:
The result seems as follows: if the Backend receives multiple Authorize.req before they reply with a confirmation to the first one, they Block all subsequent requests and accept only the first one. This scenario is not comprised within the OCPP 1.6 standard (multiple Authorize.req before Authorize.conf), therefore it is a decision of the backend to Block the subsequent requests, instead of for example to accept them all.
As I explained to Valerio, this happens only in case the Authorization via RFID has to pass through an Authorization and confirmation process with the Backend. Anther way to authorize via RFID could be to enable the local authorization list for offline scenarios. This is a solution that many Backends adopt, in order to allow local RFID authorization for example in case the connection to the Backend is offline. To do that, the Backend has to:
Enable the LocalAuthorizeOffline key
Periodically send the LocalAuthorizationList to the chargers with all accepted RFIDs.
This scenario is a normative part of the OCPP 1.6 standard, with reference to Chapter 3.5
In conclusion:
The charger correctly shows the authentication error message as it receives a Blocked Authorization form the Backend.
The above scenarios have to be discussed with the Backend. In particular, it would be interesting to understand why the Backend decided to Block the requests.
It would be also interesting to see, from Backend side, the logs related to the above authorization requests, so to understand how do they see the different incoming requests, and if they have different identifiers for each request.
Hope I provided you with a clear and exhaustive analysis in order to address the topic directly with the Backend.
Please let me know their feedback, and if further support is required form my side.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei

additional_info.subject: Status Update
additional_info.body:
Tested again on 29.01.2026 both on v8.0.5 and v8.1.4. Same behavior.
Findings:
If outlet is not selected, and IdTag scanned multiple times, charger detects the RFID and sends an OCPP Authorize request for each time it is scanned.
If outlet is selected, and IdTag scanned multiple times, charger detects the RFID and send an OCPP Authorize request only for the first scansion, then it only scans the RFID, without sending new authorize requests.
I will open a R&D technical query to understand why the different behavior.
